notes: Kinematic swimming reference for the paddle crab, keyframed by eye from blue crab footage (FASTEC clips 000106 and 000094).
Phase 0: the leading paddle upright and edge-on. Joint keys are [phase, angle_rad]; see kinematic_ref.py for conventions.
Swim direction +X (sideways, right legs leading). Paddles are the rear legs: R3 leading, L3 trailing (a mirror of R3).

v2: in the tank view the camera looks along the crab's head-tail axis, so a paddle that looks broad faces the camera (edge-on to its sideways sweep) and one that looks thin is broadside to it. Power stroke: broadside sweep over the back toward the trailing side (phase 0-0.2); recovery: feathered, rising back upright and leaning to the leading side. Both paddles tilt the same way in space; the trailing one ~0.5 rad further toward the trailing side.

v3: sweep timing matched to the footage (furthest over the back at ~0.36); trailing paddle keyed on its own, held ~45 deg toward the trailing side and moving less; leading hanging leg (R2) folds up during the sweep and hangs straight down in the recovery.

v5: per the lab, 000106 is filmed from the crab's front, slightly below (paddles at the back, away from the camera), and the crab swims toward its own left; the clip is flipped to compare with the robot swimming toward its right (+X).
v4: one reference for both clips. 000106 is filmed from behind and slightly below; 000094 from the front and above, flipped left-right so travel matches the robot's +X as seen from its front.
